name.description: Tool name (e.g. computer, navigate, find, form_input, read_page). browser_batch cannot be nested. A tabs_create's new tabId is only returned when the batch ends — load that tab in a later call.

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

actions.description: List of tool calls to execute sequentially. Example: [{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"left_click","ref":"ref_12"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"type","text":"hello"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"screenshot"}}]

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': absolute path (no ~) to the built .app bundle (e.g. /Users/me/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/MyApp-abc123/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Normative hierarchy: Charter v0 highest (contradictions reported, never resolved); spec specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.md validated and frozen, cite by section; draft branches formal/* are material only (reuse when matching the spec, divergences resolved in favor of the spec and listed).
Layout (suggested): Ern/MemoryModel/Machine.lean (Part III), Ern/MemoryModel/Access/*.lean (Parts IV-XIII, XV-XVI), Ern/MemoryModel/Arena.lean (Part XIV: arenas as reference library abstraction; O17-O19 derived over O1-O16 plus metadata; ArenaInv and the §56 guard as abstraction contract), Ern/MemoryModel/Refinement.lean (§82), Ern/Lib/HandlePool.lean, Ern/Lib/DataStack.lean (non-normative), test modules imported by no model module. MM-01 (Part II) referenced, not a module.

Obligations (all mandatory):
1. Machine (Part III). Relations total and deterministic; interpreters calculable with static obligations and WF as proof arguments; agreement theorems both ways on their domain; admissible-state invariants preserved; P1-P4, no double free, frame lemmas, read-after-write on every included sub-range (§16).
2. Kernel (Parts IV-XIII). Every operation exactly as written, including §63.8 and §77 local self-blocking prevention, §65 store rules (derived authority, free leaf, arrival-state exercisability), §72 parameter-origin rule, §73 reanchoring to the first surviving active origin, §69/§70 end of use and free, pinning rules. Locals created by entering a frame are owned directly by the frame; alloc creates exactly one root. Theorems: preservation of WF3 ∧ Inv3 ∧ AnchorOrderHeld ∧ NoOrphan by every step; reachable invariant from S3.init statics under DDSound; exitFrame_no_dangling; call_params_effective_protected; effective_exclusive; init_only_by_writes, init_statics, and the global induction (every Init leaf of a reached state was declared or written); correspondence between Step and Reachable.
3. Arena (Part XIV). issue_as_kernel, reset_as_kernel (both directions, same arrival state on the kernel part), newArena_as_library (no safety property depends on the guard), arena_reuse_safe, ArenaInv preserved.
4. Refinement (§82). Repr including MM-02 WF; R1, R2, R4, R6 for every kernel operation and derived arena operation; simulation with parameters fixed once per run; freeSound_derived; pinned_address_stable; exclusive_bytes. Decisions to apply: declared disjointness is disjointness of leaves (byte disjointness follows from layout well-formedness); a pointer to an empty region has address = base of the effective anchor's allocation and that allocation as provenance; a region's pointer address is the lowest address among its non-empty leaves; a leaf receiving a reference has pointer size (stated hypothesis, classed types/ABI).
5. HandlePool (contract: v0.4 annex). Composite borrow (companion derived from internal over the whole storage, entries derived from the companion); resolveMany Observe by Observe derivations, distinctness only in Modify; allocSlot/freeSlot require a live pool and Modify on the pool value; newPool requires Uninit storage; freeSlot ends the entry content with endUse effects, preconditions excluding internal and its ancestors; PoolInv = entry disjointness + pool_no_stale_access + transition guarantee that freeSlot never succeeds on an entry covered by an active companion descendant. Theorems: pool_resolve_modify_exclusive, pool_no_stale_access, stale/other-pool/atomicity/distinctness, pool_freeSlot_ends_content under the Modify right.
6. DataStack (contract below, identifier DS-v1). Marks carry stack identity and a fresh mark identifier; the stack keeps the ordered list of live marks; rewind m fails on a dead or foreign mark, rejects if an active authority derived from internal covers a cell above m, otherwise returns those cells to available and removes m and every mark above it; push and grow use the derived issue; grow is in place only (same base, extension into the space directly after the block, fail otherwise). Theorems: rewind_rejects_live_above, mark_no_aba (for every removed mark), rewind_keeps_older_marks, grow_same_base, grow_keeps_prefix_init, grow_keeps_prefix_bytes through the refinement.
7. Corpora. Encode MM2-H (first execution), MM3-H and MM23-H (replay) from the attached material, plus new cases: §63.8 and §77 self-blocking (reject, with twins), §56 guard, corrected HandlePool, DataStack (including ABA and a multi-stack frame scenario), W1-W3. Docstrings: model modules: every def/theorem cites the specification clause it formalizes. Library modules: cite the applicable spec clauses (§36, §56, ...) and the local contract identifier (HandlePool v0.4 annex, DS-v1), stated as non-normative.

# Report: kernel-main (Access/Main.lean, brief obligation 2)

File: `formal/Ern/MemoryModel/Access/Main.lean` (module `Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Main`, 828 lines). It
imports the six Preserve modules and is new and untracked. Nothing was committed, and no other file
was touched.

## Status

- `lake build Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Main` succeeds, and so does the full `lake build` (22 jobs,
  including the other agents' current files). `lake env lean` on the file prints nothing, so there
  are no warnings.
- `axcheck.sh Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Main` reports 193 constants and 102 theorems. The list outside
  propext and Quot.sound is `#[]`, so there is no Classical.choice.
- The AGENTS.md grep over the whole tree prints nothing. There is no `noncomputable` and no
  `set_option`.
- All 40 declarations have an English docstring that cites a § clause, checked by script. So do the
  constructors of `KernelOp`, `KStar` and `ReachableDU`. There are no draft citations, and no line is
  longer than 100 characters.
- Spec passages read in full before coding: §39, §44, §45, §47, §54, §57, §58, §59, §60–§63, §80.

## Theorems (namespace `Ern.MemoryModel.Access`)

### (e) Operations, steps, reachability, §58, §39

| Name | Statement | Clause |
|---|---|---|
| `KernelOp` (inductive) | the 16 operations O1–O16 with their arguments | §60–§75 |
| `KernelOp.Step k op` (def) | the step relation of the operation, `S3 → Outcome3 S3 → Prop` | §58, §60–§75 |
| `kstep_iff` | `KStep k s s' ↔ ∃ op, op.Step k s (.ok s')` | §57, §58 |
| `KStar k s` (inductive) | reflexive-transitive closure of `KStep` from `s` | §57 |
| `reachable_iff` | `Reachable k statics s ↔ KStar k (S3.init statics) s` | §57 |
| `op_fail_only_alloc` | `op.Step k s .fail → ∃ pr ow ls, op = .alloc pr ow ls` | §58 |
| `kstep_base` | `KStep k s s' → s'.F.getLast? = s.F.getLast?` | §39 |
| `reachable_base` | `Reachable k statics s → s.F.getLast? = some 0`, on every reachable state with no invariant needed | §39, §47 |
| `reachable_base_mem` | `Reachable k statics s → 0 ∈ s.F` | §39 |

### (a) Preservation

| Name | Statement | Clause |
|---|---|---|
| `op_preserves` | `DDSound k → KInv s → op.Step k s (.ok s') → (∀ src dst, op ≠ .transfer src dst) → KInv s'` | §57, §58, §60–§75 |
| `op_preserves_kAux` | `KInv s → KAux s → op.Step k s (.ok s') → KAux s'` for **all 16** operations, transfer included (auxiliary) | §40, §49.7 |
| `kstep_preserves` | over `KStep`: `DDSound k → KInv s → KStep k s s' → KInv s' ∨ ∃ src dst, TransferStep k src dst s (.ok s')` | §57, §58 |
| `kstep_preserves_kAux` | `KInv s → KAux s → KStep k s s' → KAux s'` (auxiliary) | §40, §49.7 |
| `op_preserves_heldAnchored` | `WF3 s → HeldAnchored s → op.Step k s (.ok s') → HeldAnchored s'` for **all 16** operations, transfer included | §44, §65, §63, §73 |
| `kstep_preserves_heldAnchored` | the same over `KStep` | §44, §57 |
| `transfer_dst_usable_of_noDangling` | `WF3 s → TransferStep k src dst s (.ok s') → NoDangling s' → s'.Usable dst` | §63.1, §54 |
| `transfer_kinv_iff` | `KInv s → HeldAnchored s → TransferStep k src dst s (.ok s') → (KInv s' ↔ s'.Usable dst)` | §57, §63 |
| `op_preserves_of_dst_usable` | `DDSound k → KInv s → HeldAnchored s → op.Step k s (.ok s') → (∀ src dst, op = .transfer src dst → s'.Usable dst) → KInv s' ∧ HeldAnchored s'` | §57, §63 |

(Restated in fix round 1, finding KM-2: no statement of this section takes `KAux` except the two
`_kAux` theorems; see `fix1-kernel.md`.)

The strongest true transfer statement is `transfer_kinv_iff`. On states with `KInv ∧
HeldAnchored`, "destination usable after" is sufficient (the Transfer module's theorem). It is also
**necessary**, because `KInv s'` already gives it through `NoDangling s'`: the §63.1 `Modify`
authority of the current frame over the destination stays active and still covers the destination's
leaves.

### (b) Reachable states

| Name | Statement | Clause |
|---|---|---|
| `reachable_kinv_false` | `¬ ∀ k statics s, DDSound k → StaticsOK statics → Reachable k statics s → KInv s`. Witness: `transfer_breaks_kinv` extended by its transfer step; `StaticsOK cycStatics` is decided. | §57, §63 |
| `KStepDU` (def) | `∃ op, op.Step k s (.ok s') ∧ ∀ src dst, op = .transfer src dst → s'.Usable dst`. The docstring says it is a hypothesis on runs, not a clause of §63 or §57. | §57, §63 |
| `ReachableDU` (inductive) | closure of `KStepDU` from `S3.init statics` | §57 |
| `ReachableDU.reachable` | `ReachableDU ⊆ Reachable` | §57 |
| `kstepDU_iff` | `DDSound k → KInv s → HeldAnchored s → (KStepDU k s s' ↔ KStep k s s' ∧ KInv s')` | §57, §63 |
| `reachableDU_kinv` | `DDSound k → StaticsOK statics → ReachableDU k statics s → KInv s ∧ KAux s ∧ HeldAnchored s`, with `KInv = WF3 ∧ Inv3 ∧ AnchorOrderHeld ∧ NoOrphan` | §57, §47 |

`kstepDU_iff` shows that the restriction is exactly "the step keeps §57". From a state where the
invariant holds, a kernel step is a `KStepDU` step iff its resulting state satisfies `KInv`. So,
by induction from `init_kinv`, `ReachableDU` is the set of states reached by runs along which §57
holds at every state. This run-level equivalence is not stated as a separate theorem.

### (c) Initial state

| Name | Statement | Clause |
|---|---|---|
| `init_kinv` | `StaticsOK statics → KInv (S3.init statics) ∧ KAux (S3.init statics) ∧ HeldAnchored (S3.init statics)` | §47, §49, §50–§54, §57 |
| `init_statics` | `(S3.init statics).I l = .init ↔ ∃ e, statics[l]? = some e ∧ e.2 = true` | §47, §59 |

### (d) Initialization (§59)

| Name | Statement | Clause |
|---|---|---|
| `KernelOp.Writes s l` (def) | write/writeShared: `l ∈ ls`; store: `l = p`; transfer: `l ∈ footprint s.P dst ∧ ∃ l' ∈ footprint s.P src, corr s.P src dst l' = some l ∧ s.I l' = .init`; every other operation: `False` | §59 |
| `init_only_by_writes` | `op.Step k s (.ok s') → s.I l ≠ .init → s'.I l = .init → op.Writes s l`, keyed on the executed operation | §59 |
| `init_history` | `KStar k (S3.init statics) s → s.I l = .init → (∃ e, statics[l]? = some e ∧ e.2 = true) ∨ ∃ t t' op, KStar k (S3.init statics) t ∧ op.Step k t (.ok t') ∧ t.I l ≠ .init ∧ t'.I l = .init ∧ op.Writes t l ∧ KStar k t' s` (an explicit run init →* t → t' →* s) | §47, §59 |

Private helpers: `heldAnchored_of_step` (the shared argument: §49.8 gives a usable holder before
the step), `getElem?_append_cases`, `initP_len`, `initP_get`, `initP_get'`, `initA_get`,
`rootIdx_get`, `statics_parent`, `statics_owner`, `init_usable`, `init_lt_of_mem_footprint`,
`init_rootPlace`, `init_root_inj`. Reused from other modules: `Frames.getElem?_inj_of_lt`,
`Frames.range_pairwise_lt`, `Frames.exists_getElem?_of_mem`, `EndFree.endUse_active`,
`EndFree.free_active`, and `Alloc.guarded_ne_fail`. No forbidden list lemma is used.

## HeldAnchored: the conjecture holds

`HeldAnchored` holds at `S3.init`, since there is no derived authority. It is preserved by every
kernel step from a `WF3` state (`op_preserves_heldAnchored`). No counterexample exists for any
operation:

- **derive, split, enterFrame, alloc:** new authorities are frame-held or have no origin.
  `enterFrame` parameters become frame-held.
- **release:** filters only the released anchor.
- **depend:** only adds anchors.
- **store:** anchors the stored authority (§65 effect).
- **transfer:** the Transfer module's theorem.
- **exitFrame:** a surviving anchor maps to itself (`firstSurv (x :: ancs x) = x`).
- **endUse:** an authority that stays active is not held within `p`, so its holder's `D` is kept.
- **free:** keeps `D`.
- **read, write, writeShared, pin, unpin:** keep `A` and `D`.

So P-T2 (Transfer report) cannot occur on `ReachableDU` states. Its counterexample `ahx` is not
reachable by such runs.

## Obligations not proved

Two items of brief obligation 2 are **not proved in the brief's form**, because they are false
under v0 (spec defect P-M1 = SP-A1, §57/§63; counterexample `transfer_breaks_kinv`):

1. "Preservation of `WF3 ∧ Inv3 ∧ AnchorOrderHeld ∧ NoOrphan` by every step": proved for every
   operation **except `transfer`** (`op_preserves`, `KInv s → step ok → KInv s'`, no auxiliary
   hypothesis). For `transfer` it fails (`transfer_breaks_kinv`); only the conditional
   `transfer_kinv_iff` (under the auxiliary `HeldAnchored`) is proved, and `kstep_preserves` is a
   disjunction.
2. "Reachable invariant from `S3.init statics` under `DDSound`": refuted
   (`reachable_kinv_false`). Only the conditional `reachableDU_kinv` (runs whose transfers keep
   the destination usable, plus `StaticsOK`) is proved.

Both are blocking for the PR under the brief's rule. Also open, and nothing needs it: whether
`HeldAnchored` holds on **every** `Reachable` state. The preservation proof uses `WF3` before the step, and `WF3` fails after the
ownership-cycle transfer.

## Readings (representation only)

1. **"Every step except transfer" over unlabelled `KStep`** is stated as a disjunction
   (`kstep_preserves`: preserved, or the step is an accepted transfer). Over the labelled
   operations it is `op ≠ .transfer` (`op_preserves`). A hypothesis such as "not a transfer step"
   on `KStep` would exclude pairs `(s, s')` that both a transfer and another operation produce.
   The disjunction avoids that.
2. **§59 "permitted write"** is keyed on the executed operation, not existentially over the
   operations relating `s` and `s'`. "Including during a derived `issue`" is covered by `store`,
   because `issue` is a library operation. The transfer disjunct is read as the draft reads it: a
   destination leaf with a corresponding source leaf `Init` before the step.
3. **§59 global form (`init_history`).** It is stated over an explicit run (`KStar`) through a
   witness step `t → t'`. It does not assert that the leaf stays `Init` after `t'`, or throughout
   in the declared case. That stronger history form was not requested.
4. **§39 "the base frame, whose identity is 0 in states reachable from the initial state, never
   exits"** is read as: the bottom of the stack is 0 on every reachable state
   (`reachable_base`). It needs no invariant, because only `exitFrame` pops a frame and §73.1
   requires a caller.
5. **§58 "only `alloc` may produce `fail`"** is stated over `KernelOp.Step`. "Leaving the state
   unchanged" holds by representation: `Outcome3.fail` carries no state. This is kernel-defs
   reading 47.
6. **`KAux` and `HeldAnchored`** are auxiliary invariants. Neither is a clause of §57. Since fix
   round 1 only `HeldAnchored` is needed by the `KInv` induction (for `transfer`); `KAux` is
   preserved separately (`op_preserves_kAux`) and kept in the conclusion of `reachableDU_kinv`. Both are discharged on the reachable states of `reachableDU_kinv`, whose
   conclusion contains `KInv` exactly.

## Problems found / for arbitration

- **P-M1 (= SP-A1 / P-T1, now at the level of §57).** §57 is false as stated
  (`reachable_kinv_false`). The witness satisfies both of §57's hypotheses, `DDSound` and
  well-formed statics. The exact repair, on states where the auxiliary invariants hold, is "the
  transfer destination is usable in the resulting state" (`transfer_kinv_iff`). This is the
  draft's dropped clause. Adding it to §63 as a precondition would make `reachableDU_kinv` the
  unconditional §57.
- **P-M2 (P-T2 resolved for these runs).** The §63.7 gap only matters on states without
  `HeldAnchored`. `HeldAnchored` is an invariant along every `KStepDU` run, so with the P-M1 repair
  §63.7 as written suffices.
- **§47 statics (P2, recorded).** `init_kinv` and `reachableDU_kinv` take `StaticsOK` as a
  hypothesis that §47 does not state. Review finding F2 notes that `StaticsOK` (`ShapeOK 0`) also
  requires owners to precede the statics they own. That is stronger than acyclicity, so it narrows
  the domain of the init theorems to declarations listed owner-first.

KW=r'^(?:@\[[^\]]*\]\s*)?(?:private\s+|protected\s+|noncomputable\s+)*(theorem|lemma|def|abbrev|structure|inductive|instance)\s+(\S+)'

+/-- An active authority with no origin is held by the owner of the root place of every leaf it
+covers (the converse of `RootHeld` restricted to active authorities), from `WF3` (§49.4, §49.7),
+`I1` (§50) and `NoDangling` (§54): the root place is usable, so its root `Modify` authority
+(§49.7) covers the leaf, and two distinct active authorities with no origin covering a common leaf
+are unrelated by derivation, so by `I1` that root authority would be `Observe`. -/
+theorem rootHeldConv_active {s : S3} (hw : WF3 s) (h1 : I1 s) (hnd : NoDangling s) :
+    ∀ (x : Nat) (z : Authority) (l r : Nat), s.A[x]? = some z → z.active = true →
+      z.origin = none → l ∈ z.footprint → RootPlace s.P r → partOf s.P l r →
+      ∃ pr, s.P[r]? = some pr ∧ z.holder = pr.owner := by
+  intro x z l r hz za zo hl hr hlr
+  obtain ⟨hlP, hleaf⟩ := hw.footprints x z hz l hl
+  have hlfr : l ∈ footprint s.P r := mem_footprint.2 ⟨hlP, hleaf, hlr⟩
+  have hur : s.Usable r := Decidable.byContradiction fun hu => hnd x z hz za r hu l hlfr hl
+  obtain ⟨i, z', pr, hz', za', zo', zm', hpr, hh', hfp'⟩ := hw.rootHeld r hr hur
+  by_cases hix : i = x
+  · subst hix; rw [hz] at hz'; cases hz'; exact ⟨pr, hpr, hh'⟩
+  · have hancs : ∀ j w, s.A[j]? = some w → w.origin = none → s.ancs j = [] :=
+      fun j w hj hw0 => by
+        have : s.org j = none := by simp [S3.org, hj, hw0]
+        simp [S3.ancs, chain_none this]
+    have := (h1 i x z' z l hix hz' hz za' za ((hfp' l).2 hlfr) hl
+      (by rw [hancs x z hz zo]; simp) (by rw [hancs i z' hz' zo']; simp)).1
+    rw [zm'] at this; cases this
+

 chains, the same footprints, and the same root authorities. -/

content.content:
## 40. Logical Places, Leaves, and Ownership

A place has an identity, optionally a structural parent, an abstract `kind`, an owner `owner : Frame | Place`, and a logical death marker. Structural parenthood `partOf(p,q)` describes the subplaces of a value; `owner` describes **who keeps the storage** of a root place valid. An owned place may lie outside its owner's direct footprint; ownership and composition are therefore distinct.

A **leaf** is a place with no structural children. `footprint(p)` contains the leaves of `p`, and access rights over a place are evaluated on those leaves. Places transitively owned by a value are not automatically leaves of its `footprint`. A logical unit of the access discipline does not automatically constitute an additional allocation in the elementary memory machine.

A place `p` is **usable** (`Usable(s,p)`) if and only if:

1. `p` exists and is not marked dead;
2. if its owner is a frame, that frame belongs to the stack;
3. if its owner is a place `q`, then `q` is itself usable and the chain terminates at a frame in the stack.

An ownership cycle makes no place usable. `placeFrame(p)` is the terminal frame of this chain when `p` is usable. Structural parts share their parent's owner and death marker. A value may be logically ended by `endUse` without the place that contained it becoming unusable; the substorages it owned may, however, die.

A **root place** has no structural parent. Every root place has a root authority of own mode `Modify`, with no origin, held exactly by that place's owner (`RootHeld`). This authority cannot be transferred in isolation; root ownership follows a legal transfer of the owning value when necessary.

## 49. WF3 — Well-Formedness of Frames, Places, and Authorities

`WF3(s)` is a **predicate on state `s`**. It jointly requires:

1. a nonempty, duplicate-free frame stack, every frame having a valid identity and, except for the base frame, a valid parent; frame-parent relations are well-founded;
2. a place structure whose composition links are valid and **acyclic**; every structural part shares its parent's owner and death marker;
3. valid owners of type frame or place, and **well-founded** ownership chains reaching a live frame for every usable place;
4. footprints consisting exclusively of leaves of existing places;
5. authorities with valid identities and modes, whose existing origins form **acyclic** chains ending at a root authority;
6. `RootChain`: every origin chain of an authority covering a leaf ends at the root of the **same structural root place** as that leaf;
7. `RootHeld`: every usable root place has its active root `Modify` authority, with no origin, held exactly by its owner;
8. holder validity: every active authority is held by a frame present in the stack or by a usable place.

Numerical ordering of identifiers, parent precedence over child in a list, and bounds on generated identifiers may be used **to represent or prove** this well-formedness in a formalization; they are not normative restrictions on place or authority identities. Preservation of `WF3` by a transition is a **required property of transitions**, not an additional clause of the state predicate. `WF3` does not impose any particular physical object layout: that belongs to refinement into the elementary memory machine.

## 50. I1 — Structural Exclusivity

For two active authorities **unrelated by derivation** covering the same leaf, their own modes must both be `Observe`. This rule also applies to leaves identified as `SharedMutable`; their particular mutation is governed by the `writeShared` contract and creates no exception to I1.

Exclusivity of **effective** modes (`effective_exclusive`) is a consequence of I1 and the definition of `effective`, not the definition of I1. On a leaf, two incompatible authorities cannot simultaneously possess incompatible effective rights. The only permitted independent ordinary coexistence is `Observe` / `Observe`.

## 51. I2 — Conservation of Rights

A derived authority covers only a subfootprint of what its origin chain permits and does not elevate its mode. Derivation and splitting restrictions do not allow duplication of an exclusive right over a leaf. Every active authority is linked to a valid origin according to state and reanchoring rules. Partial suspension follows from `effective`.

## 52. I3 — Validity of Anchors and Dependencies

Every explicit anchor of a still-usable place is valid. An operation cannot invalidate an anchor retained by a place that remains usable. Transitive propagation of dependencies from contained values does not change this obligation. Dependencies are not permissions and are insufficient to justify an access.

## 53. I4 — Consumption and Movement

A `Moved` leaf cannot be read as if it still contained its previous value. Moving a value does not preserve two copies of an exclusive authority. Initialization state and authority-exercise state are separate checks.

## 54. Anchor Ordering and Absence of Orphan Rights

`AnchorOrder` and `AnchorOrderHeld` are defined in Section 44. `NoDangling` prohibits an **active** authority from covering a leaf belonging to an unusable place; the invariant does not say that a leaf is initialized. `NoOrphan` requires every active authority held by a place to be connected to a frame in the stack through a **finite, non-repeating chain** of authorities: the first link is held by a live frame, and each active link **structurally covers the entirety** of the place holding the next link. The link need not have an effective mode over that place. `NoOrphan` guarantees neither the exercisability of all stored authorities nor freedom from blocking.

## 55. ArenaInv — Invariant of the Arena Abstraction

`ArenaInv` is an invariant of the **library contract**, not an additional predicate of kernel state. For every live arena:

- `storage` designates an existing, usable place; the footprint of `internal` is exactly the footprint of `storage`;
- `internal` is active, with own mode `Modify`, held by the arena value;
- available leaves and issued regions belong to the administered storage;
- two still-active issuances have disjoint regions; no leaf of a still-issued region simultaneously belongs to `available`;
- every still-issued block authority is a derivative of `internal` complying with exclusivity and validity rules;
- anchor and ownership restrictions are respected.

Arena entries do not, by themselves, constitute an additional storage owner. Two live arenas may cover common leaves when their `internal` authorities are distinct and their effective rights are compatible; no **global** disjointness of arena footprints is imposed.

## 56. Uniqueness of Live Administration

**An authority identity may serve as `internal` for at most one live administrative abstraction**, whether an arena, `HandlePool`, `DataStack`, or another library administrative instance. Before registering a new abstraction, its creation operation must jointly check the absence of that identity from **all relevant registries of live administrations**. Uniqueness concerns the identity of the `internal` authority, not merely possible overlap of footprints: abstractions with distinct `internal` identities are not forbidden merely because their footprints overlap. Library contracts must make the information required for this guard available to the creation operation; checking only an abstraction's own registry is insufficient.

**This guard is not a condition for any safety property in Section 57.** The effective right (Section 43, case 3) already prohibits a second issuance over leaves covered by an active block derived from the same authority. Rather, the guard preserves the **abstraction contract**: without it, simultaneous administration of the same `internal` could cause `reject` instead of `fail`, or reissue a previously released block that the first administration still considers unavailable. It creates neither permissions nor allocations and introduces no general detection of authority cycles. Its physical representation and encapsulation of library registries remain outside the kernel.

## 57. Main Invariant

\[
Inv3 = I1 \land I2 \land I3 \land I4 \land AnchorOrder \land NoDangling
\]

On states reachable from `S3.init statics` under `DDSound(K)`, the kernel guarantees:

\[
WF3 \land Inv3 \land AnchorOrderHeld \land NoOrphan
\]

`ArenaInv` (Section 55) belongs to the library abstraction: it is not included in this main kernel invariant.

I5, associated with pinned storage, remains a **specialized obligation** of `K.Pinned`, not a clause automatically implied by sequential accesses alone. This property is required for reachable states under the declared assumptions. Its correspondence with allocations and bytes requires the refinement defined below.

# VIII. Definition of Transitions and Management of Authorities

import Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Ops

/-!
# Access kernel: invariants, initial state, reachability

`WF3` (§49), `I1`–`I4` (§50–§53), `NoDangling` and `NoOrphan` (§54), `Inv3` (§57), the declared
statics and `S3.init` (§47), `StaticPinnedBottom` (§75), and reachability from `S3.init statics`
under the kernel steps O1–O16 (§57). `AnchorOrder` and `AnchorOrderHeld` (§44) are in
`Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Basic`, since operations read them.
-/

namespace Ern.MemoryModel.Access

/-! ## Root places and root authorities (§40, §49) -/

/-- Root place (§40): an existing place with no structural parent. -/
def RootPlace (P : List Place) (r : Nat) : Prop := r < P.length ∧ parentOf P r = none

/-- Decidability of `RootPlace` (§40). -/
instance (P : List Place) (r : Nat) : Decidable (RootPlace P r) :=
  inferInstanceAs (Decidable (_ ∧ _))

/-- `RootChain` (§49.6): the origin chain of an authority covering a leaf ends at a root
authority (no origin) whose footprint is the footprint of a root place containing that leaf. -/
def RootChain (s : S3) : Prop :=
  ∀ (a : Nat) (y : Authority) (l : Nat), s.A[a]? = some y → l ∈ y.footprint → isLeaf s.P l →
    ∃ x z r, (x = a ∨ x ∈ s.ancs a) ∧ s.A[x]? = some z ∧ z.origin = none ∧ RootPlace s.P r ∧
      partOf s.P l r ∧ ∀ l', l' ∈ z.footprint ↔ l' ∈ footprint s.P r

/-- `RootHeld` (§49.7, §40): every usable root place has an active root authority of own mode
`Modify`, with no origin, held by the owner of the place, whose footprint is the footprint of the
place. -/
def RootHeld (s : S3) : Prop :=
  ∀ r, RootPlace s.P r → s.Usable r → ∃ (i : Nat) (z : Authority) (pr : Place),
    s.A[i]? = some z ∧ z.active = true ∧ z.origin = none ∧ z.mode = .modify ∧
    s.P[r]? = some pr ∧ z.holder = pr.owner ∧ ∀ l, l ∈ z.footprint ↔ l ∈ footprint s.P r

/-- Auxiliary converse of `RootHeld` (§40, §49.7), not a clause of `WF3`: an authority with no
origin is held by the owner of the root place of every leaf it covers. -/
def RootHeldConv (s : S3) : Prop :=
  ∀ (x : Nat) (z : Authority) (l r : Nat), s.A[x]? = some z → z.origin = none → l ∈ z.footprint →
    RootPlace s.P r → partOf s.P l r → ∃ pr, s.P[r]? = some pr ∧ z.holder = pr.owner

/-! ## `WF3` (§49) -/

/-- `WF3(s)` (§49): one field per item of §49. Index order of parents and origins represents
acyclicity (§49, last paragraph). -/
structure WF3 (s : S3) : Prop where
  /-- §49.1: the stack is nonempty and duplicate-free, every frame below `nF`. -/
  frames : s.F ≠ [] ∧ s.F.Nodup ∧ ∀ f ∈ s.F, f < s.nF
  /-- §49.2: parent links are valid and acyclic (the parent precedes the child); a part shares
  its parent's owner and death marker. -/
  places : ∀ (q : Nat) (pl : Place) (r : Nat), s.P[q]? = some pl → pl.parent = some r →
    ∃ pr : Place, s.P[r]? = some pr ∧ r < q ∧ pr.owner = pl.owner ∧ s.dead r = s.dead q
  /-- §49.3: owner frames are below `nF`; owner places exist; the ownership chain of every usable
  place is finite and reaches a live frame. -/
  owners : (∀ (q : Nat) (pl : Place) (f : Nat), s.P[q]? = some pl → pl.owner = .frame f →
      f < s.nF) ∧
    (∀ (q : Nat) (pl : Place) (o : Nat), s.P[q]? = some pl → pl.owner = .place o →
      o < s.P.length) ∧
    ∀ q, s.Usable q → ∃ f, FrameOf s q f ∧ f ∈ s.F
  /-- §49.4: footprints consist of leaves of existing places. -/
  footprints : ∀ (a : Nat) (x : Authority), s.A[a]? = some x → ∀ l ∈ x.footprint,
    l < s.P.length ∧ isLeaf s.P l
  /-- §49.5: an existing origin precedes the authority, so origin chains are acyclic and end at a
  root authority. -/
  origins : ∀ (b : Nat) (y : Authority) (a : Nat), s.A[b]? = some y → y.origin = some a → a < b
  /-- §49.6: `RootChain`. -/
  rootChain : RootChain s
  /-- §49.7: `RootHeld`. -/
  rootHeld : RootHeld s
  /-- §49.8: every active authority is held by a frame of the stack or by a usable place. -/
  holders : ∀ (a : Nat) (y : Authority), s.A[a]? = some y → y.active = true →
    HolderLive s y.holder

/-! ## `I1`–`I4`, `NoDangling`, `Inv3` (§50–§54, §57) -/

/-- `I1` (§50): two distinct active authorities unrelated by derivation covering a common leaf
both have own mode `Observe`. -/

/-! ## §63 as written breaks `KInv` (§49.8, §54) -/

namespace TransferWitness

/-- Statics of the ownership-cycle counterexample (§47): two leaves owned by frame 0, place 0 and
place 1, both `Init`. -/
def cycStatics : Statics := [((none, none, 0), true), ((none, none, 0), true)]

/-- Initial state of the counterexample (§47). -/
def cyc0 : S3 := S3.init cycStatics

/-- After `alloc` with provider 1 and owner place 0 (§71): place 2 owned by place 0, root
authority 2 held by place 0. -/
def cyc1 : S3 := allocEff cyc0 0 [(none, 0)]

/-- After `alloc` with provider 1 and owner place 2 (§71): place 3 owned by place 2, root
authority 3 held by place 2. -/
def cyc2 : S3 := allocEff cyc1 2 [(none, 0)]

/-- After `transfer(0, 3)` (§63): place 2 is now owned by place 3, which is owned by place 2. -/
def cyc3 : S3 := transferEff cyc2 0 3

/-- `cyc2` is reached from `S3.init cycStatics` by two `alloc` steps (§57, §71). -/
theorem cyc2_reachable : Reachable Examples.K0 cycStatics cyc2 :=
  .step (.step .init (KStep.alloc (pr := 1) (ow := 0) (ls := [(none, 0)])
    (AllocStep.ok (by decide) trivial))) (KStep.alloc (pr := 1) (ow := 2) (ls := [(none, 0)])
    (AllocStep.ok (by decide) trivial))

/-- `cyc2` satisfies `KInv` and `KAux` (§57, §49.7). -/
theorem cyc2_kInv : KInv cyc2 ∧ KAux cyc2 := kInvAux_of_bounded (by decide)

/-- `transfer(0, 3)` is accepted in `cyc2`: all eight preconditions of §63 hold. -/
theorem cyc2_transfer : TransferStep Examples.K0 0 3 cyc2 (.ok cyc3) := .ok (by decide)

/-- In `cyc3`, places 2 and 3 own each other and are unusable (§40); root authority 2 is active,
held by the unusable place 3 and covers the leaf of the unusable place 2. -/
theorem cyc3_cycle : ¬ cyc3.Usable 2 ∧ ¬ cyc3.Usable 3 ∧ cyc3.Active 2 ∧
    OptP (cyc3.A[2]?) (fun y => y.holder = .place 3 ∧ 2 ∈ y.footprint) False := by decide

/-- `cyc3` violates holder validity (§49.8), so `WF3`, and `NoDangling` (§54). -/
theorem cyc3_not_wf3_noDangling : ¬ WF3 cyc3 ∧ ¬ NoDangling cyc3 := by
  obtain ⟨hu2, hu3, -, hy⟩ := cyc3_cycle
  obtain ⟨y, hy, hh, hl⟩ := optP_false_iff.1 hy
  have ya : y.active = true := by
    have : OptP (cyc3.A[2]?) (fun y => y.active = true) False := by decide
    rw [hy] at this; exact this
  refine ⟨fun hw => ?_, fun hnd => ?_⟩
  · have := hw.holders 2 y hy ya
    rw [hh] at this; exact hu3 this
  · exact hnd 2 y hy ya 2 hu2 2 (by decide) hl

end TransferWitness

open TransferWitness in
/-- §63 as written does not preserve the kernel invariant (§57, §58): under a contract with
`DDSound` (§80), from a reachable state satisfying `KInv ∧ KAux`, an accepted `transfer` reaches
a state violating `KInv` (holder validity §49.8 and `NoDangling` §54 fail,
`cyc3_not_wf3_noDangling`). -/
theorem transfer_breaks_kinv : DDSound Examples.K0 ∧ ∃ s s', Reachable Examples.K0 cycStatics s ∧
    KInv s ∧ KAux s ∧ TransferStep Examples.K0 0 3 s (.ok s') ∧ ¬ KInv s' :=
  ⟨fun _ _ h => (h : False).elim, cyc2, cyc3, cyc2_reachable, cyc2_kInv.1, cyc2_kInv.2,
    cyc2_transfer, fun h => cyc3_not_wf3_noDangling.1 h.1⟩

/-! ## The destination's usability does not suffice (§44, §63.7)

§63.7 checks `AnchorOrderHeld` only for the moved held authorities. In `ahx`, the derived
authority 6 is held by place 2, outside the transferred value, without being among its anchors
(`HeldAnchored` fails), and its effective anchor, the root 3 held by the source, moves with the
value to a younger frame. The state is not built by kernel steps: in such runs a derived
authority is held by a place only through `store` (§65), which also anchors it there. -/

namespace TransferWitness

/-- A state satisfying `KInv ∧ KAux` (§57, §49.7), not reached by kernel steps: frames 1 (current)
and 0; place 0 owned by frame 0; source place 1 owned by place 0, `Init`; place 2 owned by
frame 0; place 3 owned by the source; destination place 4 owned by frame 1. Authorities 0–4 are
the roots of places 0–4; authority 5, derived from 0, gives frame 1 `Modify` on place 0 and,
through it, on the source; authority 6, derived from the root 3, is held by place 2, with no
anchor anywhere. -/
def ahx : S3 where
  F := [1, 0]
  nF := 2
  P := [⟨none, .frame 0, 0⟩, ⟨none, .place 0, 0⟩, ⟨none, .frame 0, 0⟩, ⟨none, .place 1, 0⟩,
    ⟨none, .frame 1, 0⟩]
  I := fun l => if l = 1 then .init else .uninit
  A := [⟨.modify, none, [0], .frame 0, true⟩, ⟨.modify, none, [1], .place 0, true⟩,
    ⟨.modify, none, [2], .frame 0, true⟩, ⟨.modify, none, [3], .place 1, true⟩,
    ⟨.modify, none, [4], .frame 1, true⟩, ⟨.modify, some 0, [0], .frame 1, true⟩,
    ⟨.modify, some 3, [3], .place 2, true⟩]
  D := fun _ => []
  dead := fun _ => false
  pin := fun _ => false

/-- `transfer(1, 4)` from `ahx` (§63, `ok` effect). -/
def ahx' : S3 := transferEff ahx 1 4

end TransferWitness

open TransferWitness in
/-- With `KInv ∧ KAux` and the destination usable in the resulting state, an accepted transfer
can still break `AnchorOrderHeld` (§44, §54): in `ahx'`, authority 6 is held by place 2 of frame

fails in `ahx`. -/
theorem transfer_preserves_of_dst_usable_fails : ∃ s s', KInv s ∧ KAux s ∧ ¬ HeldAnchored s ∧
    TransferStep Examples.K0 1 4 s (.ok s') ∧ s'.Usable 4 ∧ ¬ AnchorOrderHeld s' := by
  have hk := kInvAux_of_bounded (s := ahx) (by decide)
  refine ⟨ahx, ahx', hk.1, hk.2, fun h => ?_, .ok (by decide), by decide, by decide⟩
  have := h 6 ⟨.modify, some 3, [3], .place 2, true⟩ 2 rfl rfl (by simp) rfl (by decide)
    unfold EffAnchorOK
    rw [hex, hy]
    simp only [OptP, hhq', S3.hframe, pframe_iff.2 hf]
    exact hfF
  refine ⟨kInv_of hw ⟨⟨hi1, ?_, fun _ _ x hx => ?_, i4_always _⟩, fun _ _ x hx => ?_, hnd⟩ haoh,
    hconv, fun x y q hy _ ho _ _ => ?_⟩
  · intro b y a hb ho
    obtain ⟨i, -, rfl⟩ := initA_get hb; cases ho
  · cases hx
  · cases hx
  · obtain ⟨i, -, rfl⟩ := initA_get hy; exact absurd rfl ho

/-- The `Init` leaves of the initial state are exactly the statics declared `Init` (§47, §59). -/
theorem init_statics (statics : Statics) (l : Nat) :
    (S3.init statics).I l = .init ↔ ∃ e, statics[l]? = some e ∧ e.2 = true := by
  show (if ((statics[l]?).map (·.2)).getD false then InitSt.init else .uninit) = .init ↔ _
  cases statics[l]? with
  | none => simp
  | some e => cases he : e.2 <;> simp [he]

/-! ## Reachable states (§57) -/

/-- §57 as stated is false: under a contract satisfying `DDSound` (§80) and well-formed statics
(§47), a reachable state violates `KInv`, after an accepted `transfer` (§63,
`transfer_breaks_kinv`). -/
theorem reachable_kinv_false : ¬ ∀ (k : K) (statics : Statics) (s : S3), DDSound k →
    StaticsOK statics → Reachable k statics s → KInv s := by
  intro hall
  obtain ⟨hdd, s, s', hr, -, -, ht, hn⟩ := transfer_breaks_kinv
  exact hn (hall _ _ _ hdd (by decide) (.step hr (.transfer ht)))

/-- A kernel step whose `transfer`, if it is one, leaves its destination usable (§63). The
condition is a hypothesis on runs, not a clause of §63 nor of §57. -/
def KStepDU (k : K) (s s' : S3) : Prop :=
  ∃ op : KernelOp, op.Step k s (.ok s') ∧ ∀ src dst, op = .transfer src dst → s'.Usable dst

/-- States reached from `S3.init statics` by runs whose transfers keep the destination usable
(§57, restricted by the hypothesis of `KStepDU`, which is not a clause of §63). -/
inductive ReachableDU (k : K) (statics : Statics) : S3 → Prop where
  /-- The initial state (§47). -/
  | init : ReachableDU k statics (S3.init statics)
  /-- One more step of `KStepDU` (§57). -/
  | step {s s' : S3} : ReachableDU k statics s → KStepDU k s s' → ReachableDU k statics s'

/-- From a state satisfying `KInv` (§57) and `HeldAnchored` (auxiliary) under `DDSound` (§80),
the steps of `KStepDU` are exactly the kernel steps whose resulting state satisfies `KInv`: the
restriction of `ReachableDU` keeps exactly the runs along which §57 holds. -/
theorem kstepDU_iff {k : K} {s s' : S3} (hdd : DDSound k) (hinv : KInv s)
    (hheld : HeldAnchored s) : KStepDU k s s' ↔ KStep k s s' ∧ KInv s' := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨op, hop, hdu⟩
    exact ⟨kstep_iff.2 ⟨op, hop⟩, (op_preserves_of_dst_usable hdd hinv hheld hop hdu).1⟩
  · rintro ⟨h, hk⟩
    obtain ⟨op, hop⟩ := kstep_iff.1 h
    refine ⟨op, hop, fun src dst e => ?_⟩
    subst e
    exact transfer_dst_usable_of_noDangling hinv.1 hop hk.2.1.2.2

/-- A state of `ReachableDU` is reachable (§57). -/
theorem ReachableDU.reachable {k : K} {statics : Statics} {s : S3}
    (h : ReachableDU k statics s) : Reachable k statics s := by
  induction h with
  | init => exact .init
  | step _ h ih =>
    obtain ⟨op, hop, -⟩ := h
    exact .step ih (kstep_iff.2 ⟨op, hop⟩)

/-- The main invariant of §57 (`WF3 ∧ Inv3 ∧ AnchorOrderHeld ∧ NoOrphan`, with `KAux` and
`HeldAnchored`) on the states reached by runs whose transfers keep the destination usable, under
`DDSound` (§80) and well-formed statics (`StaticsOK`, a hypothesis not stated by §47). The
restriction of the runs is not a clause of §63: without it the statement is false
(`reachable_kinv_false`). -/
theorem reachableDU_kinv {k : K} {statics : Statics} {s : S3} (hdd : DDSound k)
    (hst : StaticsOK statics) (h : ReachableDU k statics s) :
    KInv s ∧ KAux s ∧ HeldAnchored s := by
  induction h with
  | init => exact init_kinv hst
  | step _ h ih =>
    obtain ⟨op, hop, hdu⟩ := h
    have h' := op_preserves_of_dst_usable hdd ih.1 ih.2.2 hop hdu
    exact ⟨h'.1, op_preserves_kAux ih.1 ih.2.1 hop, h'.2⟩

/-! ## Initialization history (§59) -/

/-- Operation `op` writes leaf `l` from state `s` (§59): `write3` or `writeShared` of a list
containing `l`, `store` into `l`, or a `transfer` of which `l` is a destination leaf
corresponding to a source leaf `Init` before the step. -/
def KernelOp.Writes (s : S3) (l : Nat) : KernelOp → Prop
  | .write _ ls => l ∈ ls
  | .writeShared _ ls => l ∈ ls
  | .store _ p => l = p
  | .transfer src dst => l ∈ footprint s.P dst ∧
      ∃ l' ∈ footprint s.P src, corr s.P src dst l' = some l ∧ s.I l' = .init

/-- In every `ok` step, a leaf that becomes `Init` is written by the step (§59): a permitted write

# Fix round 1: kernel (KM-1, KM-2)

Branch `reference/memory-model-v0`. Nothing is committed. The full project builds with
`lake build` in `formal/` and prints no warnings. The forbidden-token grep prints nothing.
`axcheck.sh` prints empty lists for every touched module: Access.Lemmas, Access.Main,
Preserve.{Alloc, DeriveSplitRelease, EndFree, Frames, Small, Transfer} and Lib.HandlePool.

## KM-2: KAux removed from the per-step obligation (fixed)

The defect: `KAux = RootHeldConv` is not a clause of §49 or §57. It was a hypothesis of every
per-operation `*_preserves`, of `op_preserves`/`kstep_preserves` and of `exitFrame_no_dangling`.

### New lemma

`Lemmas.lean`: `rootHeldConv_active` (§49.4, §49.7, §50, §54). It derives the active, origin-less
fragment of `RootHeldConv` from `WF3 ∧ I1 ∧ NoDangling`. It is the reviewer's `conv_active`
(review2/main-preserve/kaux2.lean).

### Hypothesis replaced by I1 (a §57 clause)

The proofs applied `RootHeldConv` only to an active authority with no origin.

| Theorem | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `EndFree.endUse_noDangling` | `WF3 → NoDangling → RootHeldConv → …` | `WF3 → NoDangling → I1 → …` |
| `EndFree.free_noDangling` | same | same |
| `Frames.exit_noDangling` | `WF3 → NoDangling → RootHeldConv → OriginsSurvive → …` | `WF3 → I1 → NoDangling → OriginsSurvive → …` |
| `exitFrame_no_dangling` | `WF3 s → NoDangling s → RootHeldConv s → ExitStep … → …` | `WF3 s → I1 s → NoDangling s → ExitStep … → …` (§57 clauses only). The docstring says so. |

### Per-operation preservation: KInv split from KAux

Every operation now has `X_preserves : KInv s → step ok → KInv s'` with no `KAux` (`split` also
takes `DDSound`). The auxiliary part is a separate theorem:

| Operation | `KInv` theorem (restated) | `KAux` theorem |
|---|---|---|
| derive, split, release | `derive_/split_/release_preserves` | existing `*_preserves_rootHeldConv` (step level) |
| depend, store | `depend_/store_preserves` | existing `*_preserves_rootHeldConv` |
| read, write, writeShared, pin, unpin | `*_preserves` | new `*_preserves_kAux (haux : KAux s) (h) : KAux s'` |
| endUse, free | `endUse_/free_preserves` | new `endUse_/free_preserves_kAux` |
| enter | `enter_preserves` | new `enter_preserves_kAux (hk : KInv s) (ha : KAux s) (h)` (needs `WF3`) |
| exit | `exit_preserves` | new `exit_preserves_kAux (ha : KAux s) (h)` |
| alloc | `alloc_preserves` | new `alloc_preserves_kAux (hk : KInv s) (ha : KAux s) (h)` (needs `WF3`) |
| transfer | `transfer_preserves_wf3_inv3_of_dst_usable`: `KInv → step → dst usable → WF3 ∧ Inv3 ∧ NoOrphan` (was `… ∧ KAux`, with a `KAux` hypothesis). `transfer_preserves_of_dst_usable_of_heldAnchored`: `KInv → HeldAnchored → step → dst usable → KInv` (was `KInv ∧ KAux`, with a `KAux` hypothesis). | new `transfer_preserves_kAux (haux) (h)`. It is unconditional, with no destination hypothesis. |

The shared lemma `EndFree.releases_preserve` no longer takes `KAux` and concludes `KInv` only. A
new `EndFree.releases_preserve_kAux` covers the auxiliary part. The private helpers
`kinv_of_parts`, `write3Eff_preserves` and `pinEff_preserves` in Small.lean were narrowed the same
way.

### Main.lean

- `op_preserves`: `DDSound k → KInv s → op.Step k s (.ok s') → op ≠ transfer → KInv s'`. This is
  the brief's form for every operation except transfer.
- `op_preserves_kAux` (new): `KInv s → KAux s → op.Step k s (.ok s') → KAux s'`, for every
  operation, transfer included.
- `kstep_preserves`: `DDSound k → KInv s → KStep k s s' → KInv s' ∨ ∃ src dst, TransferStep …`.
- `kstep_preserves_kAux` (new): `KInv s → KAux s → KStep k s s' → KAux s'`. It replaces the
  `KAux` that the old first disjunct carried.
- `transfer_kinv_iff`: `KInv s → HeldAnchored s → TransferStep … (.ok s') → (KInv s' ↔ s'.Usable
  dst)`. `KAux` was dropped and `HeldAnchored` kept (auxiliary).
- `op_preserves_of_dst_usable`: `DDSound → KInv → HeldAnchored → step → hdu → KInv s' ∧
  HeldAnchored s'`. `KAux` was dropped from both the hypotheses and the conclusion. The `KAux`
  part is now `op_preserves_kAux`.
- `kstepDU_iff`: the `KAux` hypothesis was dropped.
- `reachableDU_kinv`: **statement unchanged**. Its conclusion is still
  `KInv s ∧ KAux s ∧ HeldAnchored s`. Only the proof changed: it combines
  `op_preserves_of_dst_usable` with `op_preserves_kAux`.
- `init_kinv`: unchanged.

### Statement changes beyond the four named items

- `endUse_keeps_dependents` lost its `KAux` hypothesis. It only used it to call
  `endUse_preserves`, and an unused binder would raise a linter warning. This makes the statement
  strictly stronger.
- The internal lemmas `releases_preserve`, `endUse_noDangling`, `free_noDangling`,
  `Frames.exit_noDangling` and `transfer_preserves_*` were restated as described above. They lie
  on the proof path, and no caller outside Access uses them, except `releases_preserve`.
- The hypothesis swap `RootHeldConv → I1` in the `*_noDangling` lemmas and in
  `exitFrame_no_dangling` is not a strengthening in isolation: the two hypotheses are
  incomparable. Under `KInv`, every new form is at least as strong as the old one. The old
  `RootHeldConv` forms are not kept. The task prescribes the `exitFrame_no_dangling` form, and no
  caller needs the old ones.
- The witnesses `transfer_breaks_kinv`, `transfer_preserves_of_dst_usable_fails`,
  `split_unsound_without_DD` and `cyc2_kInv` are unchanged. They still state `KAux`, which only
  strengthens them.

### Callers adapted

- `Ern/Lib/HandlePool.lean` `contentEnd_preserves`: the statement is unchanged. The proof now
  pairs `EndFree.releases_preserve` (without `ha`) with `EndFree.releases_preserve_kAux`.
- Arena.lean, Refinement.lean, RefinementArena.lean, DataStack and Corpus: no caller of a
  restated theorem, so they are unchanged and still build.

## KM-1: report wording (no code change, fixed in the record)

`reports/kernel-main.md`, section "Obligations not proved", said "None". It now lists the two
items of brief obligation 2 that are not proved in the brief's form, because both are false
under v0 (spec defect P-M1 = SP-A1):

1. Preservation by every step fails for `transfer` (`transfer_breaks_kinv`). Only
   `op_preserves` (every other operation) and the conditional `transfer_kinv_iff` (under
   `HeldAnchored`) are proved, and `kstep_preserves` is a disjunction.
2. The reachable invariant under `DDSound` is refuted (`reachable_kinv_false`). Only the
   conditional `reachableDU_kinv` is proved.

Both are marked blocking for the PR. The signature rows in sections (a) and (b) of
`kernel-main.md`, and its reading 6, were updated to the new statements. The `pres-*.md` reports
still show the old combined signatures; this file supersedes them.

## Not done / open

- `Lib/HandlePool.lean` `contentEnd_noDangling` and `contentEnd_preserves` still take
  `RootHeldConv`/`KAux`, and `xreach_inv`'s `hK` still has the shape `KInv → KAux → … → KInv ∧
  KAux`. These are library statements outside KM-2, so they are left unchanged. The same
  `rootHeldConv_active` argument would remove `KAux` from the `KInv` part of
  `contentEnd_preserves`. This is a suggestion, not done.
- The spec defect behind KM-1 (§57/§63, P-M1) is unchanged and still blocks obligation 2.

# Reading policy for the reference kernel (fixed by the orchestrator; every item is reported for arbitration)

General
- The frozen spec specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.md is the only semantic source. Cite clauses as §N or §N.k (item k).
- Formalize each clause as written. Never add a clause the text does not state (no "robustness"); never drop one.
- When a clause has no checkable content in the state (undefined term), do not invent content: omit it from the definition and record it in readings.md (clause, quote, why it cannot be formalized).
- When a clause has two readings, use the one listed below; if the case is not listed, use the draft's reading if the draft matches one of the readings, and record it in readings.md with both readings and an example of a program whose verdict changes.
- A representation choice that changes no accepted program is free (record it briefly).

State (§38): S3 = (F, nF, P, I, A, D, dead, pin). No arena registry, no callParams, no freed. Library state lives elsewhere.
Outcomes (§58): one type Outcome3 σ := ok σ | reject | fail; every O1–O16 relation except alloc never yields fail.
O1 derive (§60): takes a region (List Nat, read extensionally), not a place. Preconditions: active source; ExercisableAt source mode; every leaf of region exists, is a leaf, belongs to afp source; mode ≤ effective mode of source on each leaf; §60.3 as a decidable clause (no unrelated active authority becomes incompatible); §60.4 current frame live. §60.1c "origin chain and anchors valid" and §60.4b "footprint and anchoring restrictions": no checkable content -> omitted, recorded.
O2 split (§61): draft clauses (incl. no exclusive right already distributed). §61.4 is NOT a precondition (the §61 note says an accepted split may violate I1 without DDSound) -> recorded.
O3 release (§62): draft clauses; §62.5 (abstraction contracts) omitted, recorded.
O4 transfer (§63): draft clauses MINUS the draft's extra clause "(transferEff s src dst).Usable dst" (not in §63); PLUS §63.8 (local self-blocking prevention, as LockOptions.Opt2Transfer on formal/derivability_0.1); effect: dependencies follow the corresponding places corr(r) (not all to the destination root); §63.6 over moved usable places and AnchorOrder in the resulting state; §63.7 AnchorOrderHeld for the moved held authorities in the resulting state; §63.4 = draft ActiveDerivedOutside reading (recorded); §63.2 child order = place index order (recorded).
O5 depend (§64): draft clauses; §64.2b "real dependency" omitted, recorded.
O8 store (§65): draft clauses (they match).
O9/O10/O11 (§66–§68): add "every leaf belongs to a usable place" (§66.1, §67.1, §68.1); O10 keeps §67.2 explicitly.
O12 endUse (§69): death markers transitive over owned storage; drop the draft's extra disjunct that blocks descendants of authorities the step releases (not in §69.2) -> record the consequence.
O13 free (§70): death markers transitive; no extra "Usable p" and no clearing of D beyond what §70 prescribes; §70.4 scope = the released unit (place and storage that dies with it).
